title: Writing parametric flood triggers from a global flood model: a gauge-by-gauge test in the Guadalquivir basin, Spain
description:
A parametric flood policy pays when a river index crosses an agreed trigger. Where a river has no gauge, the index has to come from a global flood model, and the policy is only as good as the model's agreement with the floods that actually happen. We test how a trigger set from the GloFAS reanalysis performs against 14 river gauges in the Guadalquivir basin, Spain (583–16,166 km², water years 1985–2022, 286 gauge-years). Flood-frequency curves were fitted to annual maxima from both sources by L-moments (GEV and log-Pearson III), and 1-in-T triggers were scored year by year against the floods the gauges measured. The model's 10-year flood is 0.22 of the gauged one at the median gauge, so a trigger written in m³/s from the model caught only 6 of 60 1-in-5 flood years (Peirce skill 0.06, no better than chance). Written instead as the model's own 1-in-5 level, the same trigger caught 30 of 60 (hit rate 0.50, false-alarm rate 0.12, Peirce skill 0.38); 24 flood years were caught only by the return-period trigger and 0 only by the fixed-flow one (McNemar p = 1.2 × 10⁻⁷). Basis risk remained high (27 false payouts, 47% of all payouts). Across gauges, the rank correlation of annual floods between gauge and model predicted the share of flood years caught (Spearman ρ = 0.80, p = 0.0006), which gives a simple screen for basis risk wherever a short local record exists. Triggers from a global model should be written as the model's own return period and calibrated locally before they enter a contract. Data, code and a notebook that reproduces every number are published with this paper.

The record holds the research paper, a companion technical report (KAI-Hydro KH-TR-2026-01) and the data package: derived annual maxima at 14 CEDEX gauges and their GloFAS cells, the result files, the figures, a notebook that reproduces every number, and the scripts that rebuild the derived data from the sources and build the documents. Interactive version with maps: https://kai-water.charkaks0.workers.dev/case-guadalquivir.
notes: Gauge data: Fuente: CEDEX, Anuario de Aforos 2021-2022 (MITECO); raw CEDEX files are not redistributed, only derived annual maxima. Global model: contains modified Copernicus Emergency Management Service information 2026 (GloFAS 4.0), via the Open-Meteo flood API (CC BY 4.0). Code: MIT. Text, figures and derived data: CC BY 4.0. Analysis code and text were prepared with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) and checked by the author.
